title: A name that resolves to something other than what it spells is refused, never repaired
scope:
decides how Novis reads text whose *spelling* and whose *meaning* can come apart — an HTTP
message's framing and headers, inbound and outbound alike; a cookie name and its `__Host-`/`__Secure-`
prefix; a multipart body's part accounting; and a path component handed to `Core\IO::within`. Does **not**
decide which security headers a response carries or what an outbound call's deadline is
([0074](0074.md)); does **not** decide request-size caps, per-IP limits or
slow-loris timeouts, which stay a proxy's ([0074](0074.md) *Alternatives*,
as corrected below); does **not** touch `Core\Path`, which stays pure string algebra with no policy
([docs/spec/01-core-library.md](../spec/01-core-library.md) § 8); does **not** cover directional controls,
which [0087](0087.md) already refuses at every boundary.

summary.headline: Input whose spelling and meaning could come apart is refused, not cleaned up
summary.body:
Where a name could be read two ways — an ambiguously framed HTTP message, a cookie name that
only matches after case folding, a path component Windows would treat as a device — Novis
refuses the input rather than normalising or truncating it into one interpretation. The list of
what counts as ambiguous is closed and written down, so "strict" cannot grow every time someone
rereads a specification; anything not on it is merely unusual and accepted as written. HTTP is
checked in both directions, since a remote server is an attacker too.
